## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to

an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.

are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier

Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to

live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to

an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.

are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier

Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to

live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to

an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.

are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier

Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to

live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to

an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.
Liveness validation, per-conversation locking, and bounded concurrent tab allocation
are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
tabs are reused for subsequent turns and idle tabs are evicted according to
`conversation_idle_minutes`. The mapping is in memory; a process restart cannot restore
an old tab even when optional message history is persisted.

For new conversations, Qwen maintains a configurable pool of authenticated warm tabs
and replenishes it after allocation. Meta AI deliberately does not use that pool:
live testing showed that preopened Meta tabs can stall requests. Meta reuses the
authenticated browser process but opens a fresh tab for each new conversation. Both
providers retain the selected tab for explicit conversation continuation.

A crashed tab can remain referenced until a later adapter failure or idle eviction.

are tracked as performance and resilience improvements in Chapters 9 and 12.# Chapter 4 — Browser Automation

## 4.1 Current stack

The proxy uses Chromium controlled by Go's Rod library over CDP. Each enabled provider
has an isolated browser process and serialized browser access. The provider mutex is
held through page setup, UI interaction, and response collection, so only one request
per provider progresses at a time. New pages use the shared stealth setup before
navigation.

`server.headless` controls normal automation. Manual login always uses a headed browser.

## 4.2 Sessions and profiles

Manual login is initiated with `--login <qwen|metaai>` or the dashboard. After the
user completes the provider's own login UI, capture stores cookies and localStorage in
`sessions/<provider>.json`. The pool watches session changes and restores them into the
provider browser. `chrome_profile_dir` optionally supplies a durable, per-provider
browser profile.

Dashboard login uses an isolated temporary profile and a fixed browser viewport. The
server returns short-lived JPEG captures of the current page and accepts constrained
pointer, wheel, key, and text events for the current login job. A random job identifier
prevents stale dashboard clients from controlling, saving, or cancelling a replacement
browser. Frame and input routes are protected by `dashboard_secret` when configured.
Redirect locations are reduced to scheme and host so OAuth query values never reach the
dashboard. Frames and input are held only in memory for the active request and are not
persisted.

Closing the modal cancels the job. A lease also closes the browser when frame requests
stop, and save, replacement, cancellation, browser errors, and server shutdown all
release the temporary pool. Save first captures session material in memory, then
revalidates job ownership before committing it. Save is non-cancellable during this
short commit so a cancelled or replacement job cannot write the session file.

These artifacts are sensitive authentication material. The proxy does not request,
store, or submit raw passwords, and has no automatic authentication, IMAP, magic-link,
or CAPTCHA workflow.

## 4.3 Conversations

The conversation manager maps `X-Conversation-Id` values to open provider tabs. Active
